title: Auxiliary standardized eighth-power problem and local essentially smooth factorization
statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p>0, A a finitely presented k-algebra, Lambda a Noetherian geometrically regular k-algebra [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], alpha:A \to Lambda a k-algebra map and q a prime minimal over popescuIdeal(alpha) [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution]. There exist a polynomial k-algebra R=k[y_1,...,y_m] [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], compatible R-algebra structures on Lambda and a finitely presented R-algebra C, a k-algebra map beta:A \to C and an R-algebra map gamma:C \to Lambda, with gamma beta=alpha and popescuIdeal(alpha) contained in popescuIdeal(gamma). There is a nonempty finite family pi_i in R whose images lie in q, whose multiplications and squared multiplications have equal kernels on each successive quotient by the preceding eighth powers, both for R and Lambda. Each image of pi_i in C is strictly standard [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element]. Put J=(pi_i^8), R_0=R/J, C_0=C/JC and Lambda_0=Lambda/JLambda. There are a finite-presentation witness for C_0 over R_0, the induced map gamma_0 and quotient prime q_0, commuting with the quotient maps and lying over q. Either popescuIdeal(gamma_0) is not contained in q_0, or q_0 is minimal over it, dim((Lambda_0)_(q_0))=0, and the canonical map (R_0)_(q_0 \cap R_0) \otimes_(R_0) C_0 \to (Lambda_0)_(q_0) factors through an essentially smooth algebra E over (R_0)_(q_0 \cap R_0) [def-weil-pbc-essentially-smooth-ring-map; def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The carriers C and E may be represented in the universe max(u,v), where k:Type u and A:Type v.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07FJ (lemma-resolve-general), Section 07FF (section-inseparable); its proof is the 20-step argument items item-power ... item-done (lines 2671-3100), using Lemmas lemma-helper, lemma-solution-modulo, lemma-enlarge-solution-modulo, lemma-resolve-special and Elkik's Lemma lemma-elkik

proof.text: (Items item-power, item-generators, item-dimension: the integers $N$, $d$ and generators of $H_{A/k}$.) Write $H=H_{A/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], $\mathfrak h_A=\sqrt{H\Lambda}$ [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution], $S_\Lambda=\Lambda\setminus\mathfrak q$ and $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=S_\Lambda^{-1}\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The primes of $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ are the $\mathfrak q'\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ with $\mathfrak q'\subset\mathfrak q$ prime; if such a $\mathfrak q'$ contains $H\Lambda$ it contains $\mathfrak h_A$, so $\mathfrak q'=\mathfrak q$ because $\mathfrak q$ is minimal over $\mathfrak h_A$. Hence $V(H\Lambda_{\mathfrak q})=\{\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\}=V(\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q})$ and $\sqrt{H\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}}=\sqrt{\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}}=\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq]. $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], so $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is finitely generated and there is $N\ge1$ with $\mathfrak q^N\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\subset H\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power]. $A$ is of finite type over the field $k$, hence Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]; choose generators $a_1,\dots,a_t$ of the ideal $H\subset A$ (Stacks writes $H_{A/R}$ here, a misprint for $H_{A/k}$). Put $d=\dim\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FJ (lemma-resolve-general), items (item-power), (item-generators), (item-dimension) and 'Ad (item-power)', lines 2687-2694 and 2855-2858

proof.text:
(Items item-standardizer, item-elkik, item-strictly-standard, item-set-n: the algebras $B$, $C$ and the integers $c$, $e$, $n$.) Let $B=A[x_1,\dots,x_d,z_{ij}]/(x_i^{2N}-\sum_{j=1}^tz_{ij}a_j)_{i=1,\dots,d}$ ($i\le d$, $j\le t$), a $k[x_1,\dots,x_d]$-algebra of finite presentation (finitely many variables and relations over the finitely presented $k$-algebra $A$). (a) For each $j$, $A_{a_j}$ is smooth over $k$ [lem-weil-pbc-singular-ideal-localization-smooth]. In $B_{a_j}$ the $i$-th relation reads $z_{ij}=a_j^{-1}(x_i^{2N}-\sum_{l
e j}z_{il}a_l)$, so $B_{a_j}\cong A_{a_j}[x_1,\dots,x_d][z_{il}:l
e j]$ as $k[x]$-algebras (the map sending $z_{il}\mapsto z_{il}$ for $l
e j$ and inverse sending $z_{ij}$ to that expression), i.e. a polynomial algebra over $A_{a_j}\otimes_kk[x]$; this is smooth over $k[x]$ by base change of $k	o A_{a_j}$ along $k	o k[x]$, the smoothness of polynomial algebras and composition [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth]. (b) In $B$, $x_i^{2N}\in(a_1,\dots,a_t)B$, so $a_1,\dots,a_t$ generate the unit ideal of $B_{x_i}$, and $(B_{x_i})_{a_j}=(B_{a_j})_{x_i}$ is smooth over $k[x]$ [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-principal-localization]; hence $B_{x_i}$ is smooth over $k[x]$ [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-local-on-cover]. (c) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-improve-presentation] to the $k[x]$-algebra $B$: we get a $B$-algebra $C$ of finite type with a $B$-algebra retraction $ho:C	o B$ such that $C_{x_i}$ and $C_{a_j}$ (by (b), (a)) are smooth over $k[x]$ with free modules of differentials. $C$ is of finite type over the Noetherian ring $k[x]$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], hence of finite presentation [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-free-differentials-strictly-standard-power] there is $c\ge1$ such that $x_1^c,\dots,x_d^c$ are strictly standard in $C$ over $k[x]$ [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element] (take $c$ at least each of the $d$ bounds $e_0$). Put $e=8c$ and $n=N+de$. (Stacks sets $n=N+dc$; the justification of item (item-sixth-resolve) needs $\mathfrak p^nk[y]_{\mathfrak p}\subset(\pi_1^e,\dots,\pi_d^e)$ for a regular system of parameters $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d$, i.e. $n\ge d(e-1)+1$, which $N+dc$ does not give when $e=8c$; $n=N+de$ satisfies $n\ge N$ and $n\ge d(e-1)+1$, and nothing else in the proof bounds $n$, so this corrects a misprint.) Let $ ar\Lambda=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ and $E\subset ar\Lambda$ the images of finitely many $k$-algebra generators of $A$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FJ (lemma-resolve-general), items (item-standardizer), (item-elkik), (item-strictly-standard), (item-set-n), (item-set-E) and 'Ad (item-strictly-standard)', lines 2695-2716 and 2860-2871

proof.text: (Item item-NP: the solution modulo $\mathfrak q^n$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-solution-modulo] (applicable: $k$ of characteristic $p$, $\Lambda$ Noetherian and geometrically regular, $n$ and $E$ as in Step 2) there are $m\ge0$, a $k$-algebra map $\varphi:k[y_1,\dots,y_m]\to\Lambda$, with $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ and $P_0=k[y_1,\dots,y_m]_{\mathfrak p}$, such that $\mathfrak p\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, $P_0\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat, and a factorization $P_0/\mathfrak p^nP_0\to D\to\bar\Lambda$ by local homomorphisms of local Artinian rings with the first arrow essentially smooth [def-weil-pbc-essentially-smooth-ring-map], the second flat, and $E$ contained in the image of $D$. The flat local map $D\to\bar\Lambda$ is faithfully flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat], hence injective [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] (case $I=0$); we identify $D$ with its image, a $k$-subalgebra of $\bar\Lambda$. Since $D$ contains the images of generators of $A$, the map $A\to\bar\Lambda$ takes values in $D$; in particular $a_1,\dots,a_t\in D$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FJ (lemma-resolve-general), item (item-NP) and 'Ad (item-NP)', lines 2717-2733 and 2873

proof.text: (Item item-choose-pii: the parameters $\pi_i$.) The field $k$ is a regular ring [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring] and $k\to k[y_1,\dots,y_m]$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth], so $k[y]$ is a regular ring [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent] and $P_0$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] to the flat map $P_0\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ of Noetherian rings ($k[y]$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], localizations of Noetherian rings are Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]) and the maximal ideal $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, which lies over $\mathfrak pP_0$ (Step 3: $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak p\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$): the prime $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak p\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is the zero ideal of the field $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, of height $0$, so $d=\dim\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\dim P_0$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. As $P_0$ is regular of dimension $d$, $\mathfrak pP_0$ is generated by $d$ elements; multiplying them by units of $P_0$ we may take them as images of $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d\in\mathfrak p$. Their images generate $\mathfrak pP_0\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, so $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, a Noetherian local ring of dimension $d$ whose maximal ideal is generated by $d$ elements, is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] with regular system of parameters $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d$. (Stacks writes 'pi_1,...,pi_d in Lambda which map to a regular system of parameters in Lambda_q'; the elements are taken in $k[y]$, as item (item-choose-pii) says.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FJ (lemma-resolve-general), item (item-choose-pii) and 'Ad (item-choose-pii)', lines 2734-2737 and 2875-2882 (Algebra, Lemma 00ON)

proof.text: (Items item-set-R, item-modify-pii: the ring $R$ and the annihilator conditions in $R$.) Let $R=k[y_1,\dots,y_m,t_1,\dots,t_d]$ (Stacks writes $t_1,\dots,t_m$ in item (item-set-R), a misprint for $t_d$ as in item (item-set-map-R)), $\gamma_i=\pi_it_i$, $S_0=k[y]\setminus\mathfrak p$, so $S_0^{-1}R=P_0[t_1,\dots,t_d]$. Each permutation of $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d$ generates $\mathfrak pP_0$ and so is a regular sequence in $P_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]; the $\pi_i$ lie in the maximal ideal, so by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-polynomial-variables] $\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_d$ is a regular sequence in $S_0^{-1}R$. Both facts persist when the $\pi_i$ are multiplied by elements of $S_0$ (units of $P_0$). We modify $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d$ one at a time so that for $i=1,\dots,d$: $\operatorname{Ann}_{M_i}(\gamma_i)=\operatorname{Ann}_{M_i}(\gamma_i^2)$, $M_i=R/(\gamma_1^e,\dots,\gamma_{i-1}^e)R$. Suppose this holds for $i\le t_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-powers] (exponents $e,\dots,e,1$), $\gamma_1^e,\dots,\gamma_{t_0}^e,\gamma_{t_0+1}$ is a regular sequence in $S_0^{-1}R$, so $\gamma_{t_0+1}$ is a nonzerodivisor on $S_0^{-1}M_{t_0+1}=S_0^{-1}R/(\gamma_1^e,\dots,\gamma_{t_0}^e)$ and $\operatorname{Ker}(\gamma_{t_0+1})=0=\operatorname{Ker}(\gamma_{t_0+1}^2)$ there. $R$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] and $M_{t_0+1}$ is a finite $R$-module, so [lem-weil-pbc-ogoma] gives $s\in S_0$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_{M_{t_0+1}}(s\gamma_{t_0+1})=\operatorname{Ann}_{M_{t_0+1}}((s\gamma_{t_0+1})^2)$ (its case $n=1$). Replace $\pi_{t_0+1}$ by $s\pi_{t_0+1}$ (still in $\mathfrak p$; $\gamma_{t_0+1}$ becomes $s\gamma_{t_0+1}$); the conditions for $i\le t_0$ involve only $\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_{t_0}$ and are unchanged. Induction on $t_0$ gives the conditions for all $i\le d$; Step 4 still holds for the modified $\pi_i$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FJ (lemma-resolve-general), items (item-set-R), (item-modify-pii) and 'Ad (item-modify-pii)', lines 2738-2747 and 2884-2918 (Algebra, Lemmas 00NQ, 07DW, 07DV; Lemma 07FC)

proof.text: (Item item-choose-deltai: the units $\delta_i$, the elements $\lambda_{ij}$ and the enlarged $D'$.) We show by induction on $t_0\in\{0,\dots,d\}$: there are $\delta_1,\dots,\delta_{t_0}\in S_\Lambda$, $\lambda_{ij}\in\Lambda$ ($i\le t_0$) and a factorization $D\to D'\to\bar\Lambda$ by local homomorphisms of local Artinian rings, $D\to D'$ essentially smooth, $D'\to\bar\Lambda$ flat, such that with $\pi'_i=\delta_i\pi_i$: (a) $(\pi'_i)^{2N}=\sum_ja_j\lambda_{ij}$ in $\Lambda$ and the image of $\lambda_{ij}$ in $\bar\Lambda$ lies in $D'$; (b) $\operatorname{Ann}_{\Lambda/({\pi'_1}^e,\dots,{\pi'_{i-1}}^e)}(\pi'_i)=\operatorname{Ann}_{\Lambda/({\pi'_1}^e,\dots,{\pi'_{i-1}}^e)}({\pi'_i}^2)$; (c) the image of $\delta_i$ in $\bar\Lambda$ lies in $D'$. For $t_0=0$ take $D'=D$ ($D\to D$ is smooth, so essentially smooth). Throughout, $P_0/\mathfrak p^nP_0\to D'$ is essentially smooth [lem-weil-pbc-essentially-smooth-composition], so [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-enlarge-solution-modulo] applies to $D'$ in place of $D$, and each enlargement $D'\to D''$ is again essentially smooth over $D$ [lem-weil-pbc-essentially-smooth-composition], keeps (a)-(c) for the earlier indices (the image only grows), and $D''\to\bar\Lambda$ is flat local, hence faithfully flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] and injective [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction]; we identify $D''$ with its image. Inductive step, $\pi=\pi_{t_0+1}$: $\pi^N\in\mathfrak q^N\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\subset H\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ (Step 1), so in $\bar\Lambda$, $\pi^N\in(a_1,\dots,a_t)\bar\Lambda$; $\pi$ and the $a_j$ lie in $D'$ (Step 3), so $\pi^N\in(a_1,\dots,a_t)\bar\Lambda\cap D'=(a_1,\dots,a_t)D'$ [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction]: $\pi^N=\sum_ja_jd_j$, $d_j\in D'$. Lift $d_j$ to $c_j\in\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$; then $\varepsilon=\pi^N-\sum c_ja_j\in\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q^{n-N}\mathfrak q^N\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\subset\mathfrak q^{n-N}H\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, so $\varepsilon=\sum a_jc'_j$ with $c'_j\in\mathfrak q^{n-N}\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, and $\pi^{2N}=\sum_jw_ja_j$ with $w_j=\pi^N(c_j+c'_j)$, where $\pi^Nc'_j\in\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ maps to $0$ in $\bar\Lambda$ (the 'key observation' of Stacks). (The detail Stacks omits:) write $w_j=u_j/s_0$ with $u_j\in\Lambda$, $s_0\in S_\Lambda$; then $s_0\pi^{2N}-\sum u_ja_j$ is $0$ in $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, so $s_1(s_0\pi^{2N}-\sum u_ja_j)=0$ in $\Lambda$ for some $s_1\in S_\Lambda$; with $s=s_0s_1$ and $\mu_j=s^{2N-1}s_1u_j$ we get $(s\pi)^{2N}=\sum_j\mu_ja_j$ in $\Lambda$ and $\mu_j/s^{2N}=w_j$. Enlarge $D'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-enlarge-solution-modulo] with $\lambda=s$ so that some $s^{q_1}\in D'$, and replace $s$ by $s^{q_1}$ and $\mu_j$ by $s^{2N(q_1-1)}\mu_j$ (both equations persist); now $s\in D'$ and the image of $\mu_j$ in $\bar\Lambda$ is $s^{2N}\pi^Nd_j\in D'$ (Stacks writes $s^{2N}d_j$). Next, $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d$ is a regular sequence in the regular local ring $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ (Step 4, [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence]); multiplying its terms by the units $\delta_1,\dots,\delta_{t_0},s$ of $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ keeps it regular (the ideals $(f_1,\dots,f_{i-1})$ and the nonzerodivisor conditions are unchanged) [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-powers] ${\pi'_1}^e,\dots,{\pi'_{t_0}}^e,s\pi$ is a regular sequence in $S_\Lambda^{-1}\Lambda$. So on $M=\Lambda/({\pi'_1}^e,\dots,{\pi'_{t_0}}^e)$, a finite module over the Noetherian ring $\Lambda$, multiplication by $s\pi$ is injective on $S_\Lambda^{-1}M$, whence $\operatorname{Ker}(s\pi)=\operatorname{Ker}((s\pi)^2)$ on $S_\Lambda^{-1}M$, and [lem-weil-pbc-ogoma] gives $s'\in S_\Lambda$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_M((s')^qs\pi)=\operatorname{Ann}_M(((s')^qs\pi)^2)$ for every $q>0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-enlarge-solution-modulo] with $\lambda=s'$ choose $q$ and enlarge $D'$ so that $(s')^q\in D'$. Set $\delta_{t_0+1}=(s')^qs$ and $\lambda_{t_0+1,j}=(s')^{2Nq}\mu_j$: then $(\pi'_{t_0+1})^{2N}=(s')^{2Nq}(s\pi)^{2N}=\sum_ja_j\lambda_{t_0+1,j}$ with $\lambda_{t_0+1,j}\mapsto(s')^{2Nq}s^{2N}\pi^Nd_j\in D'$, which is (a); (b) is the choice of $s'$; (c) holds as $s,(s')^q\in D'$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FJ (lemma-resolve-general), item (item-choose-deltai) and 'Ad (item-choose-deltai)', lines 2748-2766 and 2920-2996 (Algebra, Lemmas 05CK, 00NQ, 07DV; Lemmas 07FC, 07FI)

proof.text: Form the base-changed standardized algebra C over the polynomial base R as in original step 7. The images of all a_j have smooth principal localizations; therefore popescuIdeal alpha is contained in popescuIdeal gamma. Finite presentation follows by base change. Choose the lifting parameters (pi_i t_i)^c. Strict standardness survives base change. If multiplication by x and x^2 have the same kernel, induct on j to see that every positive power has this kernel; apply this to the annihilator equalities from steps 5 and 6. Thus the displayed eighth-power lifting hypotheses hold.

Take the canonical quotient map gamma_0 and quotient prime q_0. Their defining commutative squares specify them uniquely. The quotient algebra is finitely presented by base change. The parameters generate the maximal ideal of Lambda_q; the pigeonhole bound q^(d(e-1)+1) is contained in their e-th power ideal. Consequently the target localization of the quotient has dimension zero. If its extended singular ideal is outside q_0 use the first alternative. Otherwise the unique prime of this localization shows that q_0 is minimal over it, giving the second alternative.

The t_i map to units after localization at the inverse-image prime, so (pi_i t_i)^e and pi_i^e generate the same local ideal. Since n=N+de is at least d(e-1)+1, the n-th powers of both maximal ideals lie in the parameter-power ideals. The local quotient problem is thus a base change of the problem over R_0[t], where R_0=P/p^nP. Use the retraction C to B. The map from B to D′[t] sends x_i to pi_i t_i and z_ij to bar(lambda_ij)t_i^(2N)bar(delta_i)^(-2N). The defining relations follow from step 6 and faithful-flat injectivity. Composing t_i to delta_i gives the original map. The algebra D′[t] is essentially smooth over R_0[t]: write D′ as a localization of a smooth R_0-algebra and base change that presentation. Base change again to the local parameter-power quotient P to obtain E and the displayed local factorization. Smoothness survives base change and localization commutes with base change, so E is essentially smooth over P.

Pad the parameter list by a final zero if it is empty. Zero has equal annihilators for all positive powers and is strictly standard: use any finite presentation, take c=0 and all minor coefficients zero; the chosen polynomial lift of zero lies in the relation ideal, so its product with each relation lies in the square. This padding leaves the power ideal and all quotient maps unchanged. Represent C and E in Type(max u v) using their finite polynomial presentations and localizations; transport their structures and maps across the resulting isomorphisms.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_popescu_char_p_preparation
    {k : Type u} {A : Type v} {Λ : Type w}
    [Field k] [CommRing A] [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k A] [Algebra k Λ]
    [FinitePresentation k A] [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p)
    (α : A →ₐ[k] Λ) (q : PrimeSpectrum Λ)
    (hreg : IsGeometricallyRegular k Λ)
    (hminimal : q.asIdeal ∈ (popescuIdeal α).minimalPrimes) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (_ : Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) Λ)
      (_ : IsScalarTower k (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) Λ)
      (C : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra k C)
      (_ : Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) C)
      (_ : IsScalarTower k (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) C)
      (_ : FinitePresentation (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) C)
      (β : A →ₐ[k] C) (γ : C →ₐ[MvPolynomial (Fin m) k] Λ),
      (γ.restrictScalars k).comp β = α ∧ popescuIdeal α ≤ popescuIdeal γ ∧
      ∃ (r : ℕ) (π : Fin r → MvPolynomial (Fin m) k),
        1 ≤ r ∧
        (∀ i, algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) Λ (π i) ∈ q.asIdeal) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin r)
          (x : MvPolynomial (Fin m) k ⧸ Ideal.span
            {y | ∃ j : Fin r, j.val < i.val ∧ y = π j ^ 8}),
          π i • x = 0 ↔ π i ^ 2 • x = 0) ∧
        (∀ (i : Fin r)
          (x : Λ ⧸ Ideal.span
            {y | ∃ j : Fin r, j.val < i.val ∧
              y = algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) Λ (π j) ^ 8}),
          π i • x = 0 ↔ π i ^ 2 • x = 0) ∧
        (∀ i, IsStrictlyStandardElement
          (R := MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) C (π i))) ∧
        let R := MvPolynomial (Fin m) k
        let J := Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin r ↦ π i ^ 8))
        let J_C := J.map (algebraMap R C)
        let J_Λ := J.map (algebraMap R Λ)
        let R₀ := R ⧸ J
        let C₀ := C ⧸ J_C
        let Λ₀ := Λ ⧸ J_Λ
        ∃ (_ : FinitePresentation R₀ C₀) (γ₀ : C₀ →ₐ[R₀] Λ₀)
          (q₀ : PrimeSpectrum Λ₀),
          γ₀.toRingHom.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk J_C) =
            (Ideal.Quotient.mk J_Λ).comp γ.toRingHom ∧
          PrimeSpectrum.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk J_Λ) q₀ = q ∧
          (¬ popescuIdeal γ₀ ≤ q₀.asIdeal ∨
            q₀.asIdeal ∈ (popescuIdeal γ₀).minimalPrimes ∧
            ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime q₀.asIdeal) = 0 ∧
            let P := Localization.AtPrime (q₀.asIdeal.under R₀)
            let L := Localization.AtPrime q₀.asIdeal
            letI := Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver
              (q₀.asIdeal.under R₀) q₀.asIdeal
